Definition: ("scandal"); probably from a derivative of G2578; a trap-stick (bent sapling), i.e. snare (figuratively, cause of displeasure or sin):--occasion to fall (of stumbling), offence, thing that offends, stumblingblock.
BiblicalUsage: Skandalon is the trap-stick, the snare, the stumbling block, and it is the offence of the cross itself. Christ crucified is a stumbling block to the Jews and foolishness to the Greeks, offences will come but woe to the man through whom they come, and the doctrine of Balaam cast a stumbling block before Israel to eat things sacrificed to idols.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the cross is a stumbling block to everyone who wants a Saviour without offence. I hold that the offence is the point, because a Christ who offends no one saves no one.
